title: Simultaneous Equations Calculator: how it works, formula and examples

content:
The [Simultaneous Equations Calculator](/simultaneous-equations-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Solve two linear equations in x and y, including inconsistent and dependent systems. Enter your equation 1: a, b, c for ax + by = c and equation 2: a, b, c for ax + by = c and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Two simultaneous linear equations describe two straight lines in the xy-plane. Their intersection, if unique, is the ordered pair that satisfies both equations. Enter each in standard form and this solver applies Cramer's rule, verifies the solution by substitution, and distinguishes systems with no solution from dependent equations with infinitely many solutions. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers.

## How to use the Simultaneous Equations Calculator

Start by typing or pasting your equation 1: a, b, c for ax + by = c, then typing or pasting your equation 2: a, b, c for ax + by = c. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause.

1. Rearrange each equation as ax + by = c, moving constants to the right-hand side.
2. Enter a, b and c in order for both equations, preserving negative signs.
3. Check x and y in the original equations and read the determinant if the system has no unique intersection.

## Formula

D = ae − bd, Dx = ce − bf and Dy = af − cd for a₁x+b₁y=c₁ and a₂x+b₂y=c₂. If D ≠ 0, x = Dx/D and y = Dy/D.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Simultaneous Equations Calculator](/simultaneous-equations-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. For 2x + 3y = 13 and 4x − y = 5, D = −14, Dx = −28 and Dy = −42. Therefore x = 2 and y = 3; substitution gives 13 and 5 respectively. Try the same figures in the [Simultaneous Equations Calculator](/simultaneous-equations-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Equation 1: a, b, c for ax + by = c: 2, 3, 13, Equation 2: a, b, c for ax + by = c: 4, -1, 5), the [Simultaneous Equations Calculator](/simultaneous-equations-calculator) returns x: 2, y: 3, Solution type: One unique solution, Coefficient determinant: -14, Check equation 1: 13 = 13, Check equation 2: 5 = 5. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Percentage Calculator](/percentage-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## Three possible outcomes

Non-parallel lines meet once and produce a unique solution. Distinct parallel lines never meet, so the equations are inconsistent. Coincident lines represent the same set of points and produce infinitely many solutions. The coefficient determinant separates the first case from the other two; the numerator determinants then distinguish dependence from inconsistency.

## Why standard form matters

For y = 2x + 5, rearrange to −2x + y = 5 before entering coefficients. A common error is entering the slope as a while leaving y on the left with the wrong sign. Fractions can be entered as decimals, but keeping exact values until the final step reduces rounding differences.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Move every constant to the right before extracting a, b and c.
- A coefficient of zero must still be entered to keep all three positions.
- Use the substitution checks to catch sign and entry mistakes.

## Frequently asked questions

### What does a zero determinant mean?

The equations do not have one unique intersection. They either describe parallel distinct lines with no solution or the same line with infinitely many solutions. Try it with your own numbers in the [Simultaneous Equations Calculator](/simultaneous-equations-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Can I solve equations with decimals?

Yes. Integer and decimal coefficients are supported. Results may be rounded for display, so retain full precision in later work when needed. Try it with your own numbers in the [Simultaneous Equations Calculator](/simultaneous-equations-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Does this handle three variables?

No. This page is specifically for two linear equations in x and y; larger systems require a matrix or general linear-system solver. Try it with your own numbers in the [Simultaneous Equations Calculator](/simultaneous-equations-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Simultaneous Equations Calculator use?
